**Q3 2026 revenue:** Equinix had not yet reported Q3 as of October 17, 2026; it scheduled its earnings call for October 28, so the relevant company figure is its Q3 revenue guide of **$2.525–$2.575 billion** (midpoint **$2.550 billion**), representing **9–11% year-over-year reported growth** and **10–12% normalized/constant-currency growth**. [[1, 2]] 
The available analyst consensus was **$2.618 billion**, about **$43 million (1.7%) above** the high end of management’s range and **2.7% above** its midpoint, implying the principal near-term revenue-execution risk was expectations above formal guidance. [[3, 2]]

**Why AI demand appears material:** In Q2, Equinix said AI infrastructure demand was accelerating and that the vast majority of its largest deals were AI-workload driven; management characterized the demand as spanning private AI stacks, sovereign deployments, batch training/inference, and latency-sensitive inference. [[4]] 
This is not solely a hyperscaler-compute story: Equinix’s differentiated proposition is neutral, connected infrastructure, and the company stated that eight of the top 10 AI model providers and eight of the top 10 neoclouds use its platform for key networking workloads. [[4]]

**xScale leasing read-through:** The clearest quantitative evidence is **134 MW of xScale leasing signed across the Americas in Q2 2026**; its xScale portfolio totaled **604 MW leased**, with approximately **2,000 MW of capacity when fully built out** and more than **$23 billion** of total investment. [[5]] 
That leasing was financially consequential: Q2 revenue was **$2.625 billion**, up **16% year over year**, and management explicitly attributed part of that growth to one-time xScale fees; the Hampton xScale transaction alone contributed about **$120 million** of non-recurring fees. [[2, 6]] 
Accordingly, xScale validates substantial AI/hyperscale demand and supports future capacity utilization, but investors should distinguish recurring underlying demand from the timing volatility created by non-recurring leasing fees. [[2, 6]]

**Interconnection is the stronger recurring-demand indicator:** Equinix delivered **$424 million of annualized gross bookings**, up **23% year over year**, and added a record **9,700 net interconnections** in Q2. [[2]]

events.content: Equinix Q2 2026 revenue AI xScale interconnection gross bookings net interconnections annualized

**Equinix Q2 2026 snapshot:** Revenue was **$2.625 billion**, up **16% year over year** on both a reported and normalized constant-currency basis, with strong core performance and one-time **xScale** fees contributing to growth. [[1]]

- **AI demand:** Equinix said it expanded its Cisco and NVIDIA collaboration to help enterprises deploy AI through standardized AI-factory architectures, secure infrastructure and testing environments across its global data-center footprint. [[1]]
- **xScale:** The company closed **134 MW** of xScale leases in the quarter; the Hampton transaction accounted for approximately **$120 million** of fees. [[2]]
- **Interconnection revenue:** Q2 interconnection revenue was **$256 million**, versus $251 million in Q1 2026 and $231 million in Q2 2025. [[1]]
- **Annualized gross bookings:** Equinix delivered **$424 million**, up **23% year over year**, its second-highest quarterly volume on record and a contributor to record backlog. [[1]]
- **Net interconnections:** Equinix added a quarterly-record **9,700 net interconnections**, reinforcing the platform’s interconnection momentum. [[1]]
- **Underlying recurring growth:** Monthly recurring revenue increased **11% year over year** on both reported and normalized constant-currency bases, marking the third consecutive quarter of double-digit MRR growth. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: Equinix Q1 2026 earnings results revenue AI xScale leasing interconnection

events.content: Equinix Q1 2026 earnings results revenue AI xScale leasing interconnection

**Q1 2026 revenue:** Equinix reported revenue of **$2.444 billion** for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, up **10% year over year** as reported and **8%** on a normalized, constant-currency basis. [[1]]

**AI demand / leasing:** The company delivered **$378 million of annualized gross bookings** and roughly **$140 million of annualized presales**—a record presales level—with approximately **60% of its largest deals AI-related**. [[1]]

**xScale timing:** Q1 revenue and results **did not include the Hampton xScale lease transaction**; Equinix said that, excluding the timing effect of that deal, Q1 performance was above the midpoint of its Q1 revenue-guidance range. [[1]]

**Read-through:** The deferred xScale lease is a timing issue rather than evidence of weak underlying demand, as management indicated it was negotiating expanded mutually beneficial terms and expected the associated economics to be reflected in Q2 guidance. [[2]]

**Important nuance:** Equinix did not disclose a stand-alone dollar amount for “AI leasing” revenue in Q1; the clearest disclosed AI indicators are the AI mix of large deals, the record bookings/presales, and the postponed Hampton xScale transaction. [[1]]
